newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE INCHES DOWN, SEEN REBOUNDING BRIEFLY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE INCHES DOWN, SEEN REBOUNDING BRIEFLY.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse eased in lower turnover on Monday, but analysts expected a brief rebound in reaction to last three-session 6.6 percent tumble before further falls or the market's stabilisation.
Analysts said the recent underperformance by bourse heavyweights signalled foreign investors were holding back with purchases in Warsaw, apparently waiting for better bargains.

"It seems domestic investors are active while foreigners wait for deeper falls...and although domestic demand could spur a several-day uptrend I'm not optimistic in longer-term," said Sebastian Buczek, an analyst at ING BSK Asset Management.

Analysts said Monday's news that consumer prices rose 1.1 percent in February bringing year-on-year inflation down to 17.3 percent was good news, but said they were not expecting a rate-cut earlier than in the second half of the year.
The main market's WIG index eased 0.2 percent, to 16,646.0, and trade fell 38 percent to 143.8 million zlotys on all three markets as 37 issues rose, 33 fell and 20 were flat.
Analysts said cooling down on some of world's leading stock exchanges was also negatively influencing the Polish market.
They also said Poland's forthcoming parliamentary elections were increasing investment risk and might cool investor mood.
Analysts believed 16,500 should provide strong support for the WIG index.
Izolacja started trade on the bourse's main market 37.9 percent above issue and analysts said the company's ratios signalled some upside potential.
Espebepe , which did not trade after price fixing due to excess supply, plunged 9.4 percent after a decision on its possible debt write-off deal was postponed until April 14.
Continuous trade turnover was at 17.5 million zlotys with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,696 points, 2.1 percent higher than in the regular session. -Malgorzata Rzepka +48 22 653 9700
